verses.zh: 「此后，我们转回，从红海的路往旷野去，是照耶和华所吩咐我的。我们在西珥山绕行了许多日子。
verses.en: Then we turned and set out toward the wilderness on the way to the Red Sea[NOTE:1] just as the Lord told me to do, detouring around Mount Seir for a long time.
notes: Heb “Reed Sea.” See note on the term “Red Sea” in Deut 1:40.

verses.zh: 耶和华对我说：
verses.en: At this point the Lord said to me,

verses.zh: 『你们绕行这山的日子够了，要转向北去。
verses.en: “You have circled around this mountain long enough; now turn north.

verses.zh: 你吩咐百姓说：你们弟兄以扫的子孙住在西珥，你们要经过他们的境界。他们必惧怕你们，所以你们要分外谨慎。
verses.en: Instruct[NOTE:1] these people as follows: ‘You are about to cross the border of your relatives[NOTE:2] the descendants of Esau,[NOTE:3] who inhabit Seir. They will be afraid of you, so watch yourselves carefully.
notes: Heb “command” (so KJV, NASB); NRSV “charge the people as follows.”
Heb “brothers”; NAB “your kinsmen.”

The descendants of Esau (Heb “sons of Esau”; the phrase also occurs in 2:8, 12, 22, 29). These are the inhabitants of the land otherwise known as Edom, south and east of the Dead Sea. Jacob’s brother Esau had settled there after his bitter strife with Jacob (Gen 36:1-8). “Edom” means “reddish,” probably because of the red sandstone of the region, but also by popular etymology because Esau, at birth, was reddish (Gen 25:25).

verses.zh: 不可与他们争战；他们的地，连脚掌可踏之处，我都不给你们，因我已将西珥山赐给以扫为业。
verses.en: Do not be hostile toward them, because I am not giving you any of their land, not even a footprint, for I have given Mount Seir[NOTE:1] as an inheritance for Esau.
notes: Mount Seir is synonymous with Edom.

verses.zh: 你们要用钱向他们买粮吃，也要用钱向他们买水喝。
verses.en: You may purchase[NOTE:1] food to eat and water to drink from them.
notes: Heb includes “with silver.”

verses.zh: 因为耶和华―你的　神在你手里所办的一切事上已赐福与你。你走这大旷野，他都知道了。这四十年，耶和华―你的　神常与你同在，故此你一无所缺。』
verses.en: All along the way I, the Lord your God,[NOTE:1] have blessed your every effort.[NOTE:2] I have[NOTE:3] been attentive to[NOTE:4] your travels through this great wilderness. These 40 years I have[NOTE:5] been with you; you have lacked nothing.’”
notes: The Hebrew text does not have the first person pronoun; it has been supplied for purposes of English style (the Lord is speaking here).
Heb “all the work of your hands.”
Heb “he has.” This has been converted to first person in the translation in keeping with English style.
Heb “known” (so ASV, NASB); NAB “been concerned about.”
Heb “the Lord your God has.” This has been replaced in the translation by the first person pronoun (“I”) in keeping with English style.

verses.zh: 「于是，我们离了我们弟兄以扫子孙所住的西珥，从亚拉巴的路，经过以拉他、以旬・迦别，转向摩押旷野的路去。
verses.en: So we turned away from our relatives[NOTE:1] the descendants of Esau, the inhabitants of Seir, turning from the route of the rift valley[NOTE:2] which comes up from[NOTE:3] Elat[NOTE:4] and Ezion Geber,[NOTE:5] and traveling the way of the wilderness of Moab.
notes: Or “brothers”; NRSV “our kin.”

As a geographic feature the rift valley (עֲרָבָה, ʿaravah) extends from the Gulf of Aqaba to Galilee. Traveling up the middle of the rift valley probably would have been the easiest path, at least up to the Dead Sea.
Heb “from.”

Elat was a port city at the head of the eastern arm of the Red Sea, that is, the Gulf of Aqaba (or Gulf of Eilat). Solomon (1 Kgs 9:28), Uzziah (2 Kgs 14:22), and Ahaz (2 Kgs 16:5-6) used it as a port but eventually it became permanently part of Edom. It may be what is known today as Tell el-Kheleifeh. Modern Eilat is located farther west along the northern coast. See G. Pratico, “Nelson Glueck’s 1938-1940 Excavations at Tell el-Kheleifeh: A Reappraisal,” BASOR 259 (1985): 1-32.

Ezion Geber. A place near the Gulf of Aqaba, Ezion-geber must be distinguished from Elat (cf. 1 Kgs 9:26-28; 2 Chr 8:17-18). It was, however, also a port city (1 Kgs 22:48-49). It may be the same as the modern site Gezirat al-Fauran, 15 mi (24 km) south-southwest from Tell el-Kheleifah.

verses.zh: 耶和华吩咐我说：『不可扰害摩押人，也不可与他们争战。他们的地，我不赐给你为业，因我已将亚珥赐给罗得的子孙为业。』
verses.en: Then the Lord said to me, “Do not harass Moab and provoke them to war, for I will not give you any of their land as your territory. This is because I have given Ar[NOTE:1] to the descendants of Lot[NOTE:2] as their possession.
notes: Ar was a Moabite city on the Arnon River east of the Dead Sea. It is mentioned elsewhere in the “Book of the Wars of Yahweh” (Num 21:15; cf. 21:28; Isa 15:1). Here it is synonymous with the whole land of Moab.

The descendants of Lot. Following the destruction of the cities of the plain, Sodom and Gomorrah, as God’s judgment, Lot fathered two sons by his two daughters, namely, Moab and Ammon (Gen 19:30-38). Thus, these descendants of Lot in and around Ar were the Moabites.

verses.zh: （先前，有以米人住在那里，民数众多，身体高大，像亚衲人一样。
verses.en: (The Emites[NOTE:1] used to live there, a people as powerful, numerous, and tall as the Anakites.
notes: Emites. These giant people, like the Anakites (Deut 1:28), were also known as Rephaites (v. 11). They appear elsewhere in the narrative of the invasion of the kings of the east where they are said to have lived around Shaveh Kiriathaim, perhaps 9 to 11 mi (15 to 18 km) east of the north end of the Dead Sea (Gen 14:5).

verses.zh: 这以米人像亚衲人；也算为利乏音人；摩押人称他们为以米人。
verses.en: These people, as well as the Anakites, are also considered Rephaites;[NOTE:1] the Moabites call them Emites.
notes: Rephaites. The earliest reference to this infamous giant race is, again, in the story of the invasion of the eastern kings (Gen 14:5). They lived around Ashteroth Karnaim, probably modern Tel Ashtarah (cf. Deut 1:4), in the Bashan plateau east of the Sea of Galilee. Og, king of Bashan, was a Rephaite (Deut 3:11; Josh 12:4; 13:12). Other texts speak of them or their kinfolk in both Transjordan (Deut 2:20; 3:13) and Canaan (Josh 11:21-22; 14:12, 15; 15:13-14; Judg 1:20; 1 Sam 17:4; 1 Chr 20:4-8). They also appear in extra-biblical literature, especially in connection with the city state of Ugarit. See C. L’Heureux, “Ugaritic and Biblical Rephaim,” HTR 67 (1974): 265-74.

verses.zh: 先前，何利人也住在西珥，但以扫的子孙将他们除灭，得了他们的地，接着居住，就如以色列在耶和华赐给他为业之地所行的一样。）
verses.en: Previously the Horites[NOTE:1] lived in Seir, but the descendants of Esau dispossessed and destroyed them and settled in their place, just as Israel did to the land it came to possess, the land the Lord gave them.)[NOTE:2]
notes: Horites. Most likely these are the same as the well-known people of ancient Near Eastern texts described as Hurrians. They were geographically widespread and probably non-Semitic. Genesis speaks of them as the indigenous peoples of Edom that Esau expelled (Gen 36:8-19, 31-43) and also as among those who confronted the kings of the east (Gen 14:6).
Most modern English versions, beginning with the ASV (1901), regard vv. 10-12 as parenthetical to the narrative.

verses.zh: 现在，起来过撒烈溪！于是我们过了撒烈溪。
verses.en: Now, get up and cross the Wadi Zered.”[NOTE:1] So we did so.[NOTE:2]
notes: Wadi Zered. Now known as Wadi el-Ḥesa, this valley marked the boundary between Moab to the north and Edom to the south.
Heb “we crossed the Wadi Zered.” This has been translated as “we did so” for stylistic reasons, to avoid redundancy.

verses.zh: 自从离开加低斯・巴尼亚，到过了撒烈溪的时候，共有三十八年，等那世代的兵丁都从营中灭尽，正如耶和华向他们所起的誓。
verses.en: Now the length of time it took for us to go from Kadesh Barnea to the crossing of Wadi Zered was thirty-eight years, time for all the military men of that generation to die, just as the Lord had vowed to them.

verses.zh: 耶和华的手也攻击他们，将他们从营中除灭，直到灭尽。
verses.en: Indeed, it was the very hand of the Lord that eliminated them from within[NOTE:1] the camp until they were all gone.
notes: Heb “from the middle of.” Although many recent English versions leave this expression untranslated, the point seems to be that these soldiers did not die in battle but “within the camp.”

verses.zh: 「兵丁从民中都灭尽死亡以后，
verses.en: So it was that after all the military men had been eliminated from the community,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and it was when they were eliminated, all the men of war, to die from the midst of the people.”

verses.zh: 耶和华吩咐我说：
verses.en: the Lord said to me,

verses.zh: 『你今天要从摩押的境界亚珥经过，
verses.en: “Today you are going to cross the border of Moab, that is, of Ar.[NOTE:1]
notes: Ar. See note on this word in Deut 2:9.

verses.zh: 走近亚扪人之地，不可扰害他们，也不可与他们争战。亚扪人的地，我不赐给你们为业，因我已将那地赐给罗得的子孙为业。』
verses.en: But when you come close to the Ammonites, do not harass or provoke them because I am not giving you any of the Ammonites’ land as your possession; I have already given it to Lot’s descendants[NOTE:1] as their possession.”
notes: Lot’s descendants. See note on this phrase in Deut 2:9.

verses.zh: （那地也算为利乏音人之地，先前利乏音人住在那里，亚扪人称他们为散送冥。
verses.en: (That also is considered to be a land of the Rephaites.[NOTE:1] The Rephaites lived there originally; the Ammonites call them Zamzummites.[NOTE:2]
notes: Rephaites. See note on this word in Deut 2:11.
Zamzummites. Just as the Moabites called Rephaites by the name Emites, the Ammonites called them Zamzummites (or Zazites; Gen 14:5).

verses.zh: 那民众多，身体高大，像亚衲人一样，但耶和华从亚扪人面前除灭他们，亚扪人就得了他们的地，接着居住。
verses.en: They are a people as powerful, numerous, and tall as the Anakites. But the Lord destroyed the Rephaites[NOTE:1] in advance of the Ammonites,[NOTE:2] so they dispossessed them and settled down in their place.
notes: Heb “them”; the referent (the Rephaites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “them”; the referent (the Ammonites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 正如耶和华从前为住西珥的以扫子孙将何利人从他们面前除灭、他们得了何利人的地、接着居住一样，直到今日。
verses.en: This is exactly what he did for the descendants of Esau who lived in Seir when he destroyed the Horites before them so that they could dispossess them and settle in their area to this very day.

verses.zh: 从迦斐托出来的迦斐托人将先前住在乡村直到迦萨的亚卫人除灭，接着居住。）
verses.en: As for the Avvites[NOTE:1] who lived in settlements as far west as Gaza, Caphtorites[NOTE:2] who came from Crete[NOTE:3] destroyed them and settled down in their place.)
notes: Avvites. Otherwise unknown, these people were probably also Anakite (or Rephaite) giants who lived in the lower Mediterranean coastal plain until they were expelled by the Caphtorites.

Caphtorites. These peoples are familiar from both the OT (Gen 10:14; 1 Chr 1:12; Jer 47:4; Amos 9:7) and ancient Near Eastern texts (Miriam Lichtheim, Ancient Egyptian Literature, 2:37-38; ANET 138). They originated in Crete (OT “Caphtor”) and are identified as the ancestors of the Philistines (Gen 10:14; Jer 47:4).
Heb “Caphtor”; the modern name of the island of Crete is used in the translation for clarity (cf. NCV, TEV, NLT).

verses.zh: 你们起来前往，过亚嫩谷；我已将亚摩利人希实本王西宏和他的地交在你手中，你要与他争战，得他的地为业。
verses.en: “Get up, make your way across Wadi Arnon. Look, I have already delivered over to you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon,[NOTE:1] and his land. Go ahead—take it! Engage him in war!
notes: Heshbon is the name of a prominent site (now Tel Hesbān, about 7.5 mi [12 km] south southwest of Amman, Jordan). Sihon made it his capital after having driven Moab from the area and forced them south to the Arnon (Num 21:26-30). Heshbon is also mentioned in Deut 1:4.

verses.zh: 从今日起，我要使天下万民听见你的名声都惊恐惧怕，且因你发颤伤恸。」
verses.en: This very day I will begin to fill all the people of the earth[NOTE:1] with dread and to terrify them when they hear about you. They will shiver and shake in anticipation of your approach.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “under heaven” (so NIV, NRSV).
Heb “from before you.”

verses.zh: 「我从基底莫的旷野差遣使者去见希实本王西宏，用和睦的话说：
verses.en: Then I sent messengers from the Kedemoth[NOTE:1] wilderness to King Sihon of Heshbon with an offer of peace:
notes: Kedemoth. This is probably Aleiyan, about 8 mi (13 km) north of the Arnon and between Dibon and Mattanah.

verses.zh: 『求你容我从你的地经过，只走大道，不偏左右。
verses.en: “Let us pass through your land; we will keep strictly to the roadway.[NOTE:1] We will not turn aside to the right or the left.
notes: Heb “in the way in the way” (בַּדֶּרֶךְ בַּדֶּרֶךְ, badderekh badderekh). The repetition lays great stress on the idea of resolute determination to stick to the path. IBHS 116 §7.2.3c.

verses.zh: 你可以卖粮给我吃，也可以卖水给我喝，只要容我步行过去，
verses.en: Sell us food for cash[NOTE:1] so that we can eat and sell us water to drink.[NOTE:2] Just allow us to go through on foot,
notes: Heb “silver.”
Heb “and water for silver give to us so that I may drink.”

verses.zh: 就如住西珥的以扫子孙和住亚珥的摩押人待我一样，等我过了约旦河，好进入耶和华―我们　神所赐给我们的地。』
verses.en: just as the descendants of Esau who live at Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for us, until we cross the Jordan to the land the Lord our God is giving us.”

verses.zh: 但希实本王西宏不容我们从他那里经过；因为耶和华―你的　神使他心中刚硬，性情顽梗，为要将他交在你手中，像今日一样。
verses.en: But King Sihon of Heshbon was unwilling to allow us to pass near him because the Lord our[NOTE:1] God had made him obstinate[NOTE:2] and stubborn[NOTE:3] so that he might deliver him over to you[NOTE:4] this very day.
notes: The translation follows the LXX in reading the first person pronoun. The MT, followed by many English versions, has a second person masculine singular pronoun, “your.”
Heb “hardened his spirit” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV); NIV “made his spirit stubborn.”
Heb “made his heart obstinate” (so KJV, NASB); NRSV “made his heart defiant.”
Heb “into your hand.”

verses.zh: 耶和华对我说：『从此起首，我要将西宏和他的地交给你；你要得他的地为业。』
verses.en: The Lord said to me, “Look! I have already begun to give over Sihon and his land to you. Start right now to take his land as your possession.”

verses.zh: 那时，西宏和他的众民出来攻击我们，在雅杂与我们交战。
verses.en: When Sihon and all his troops[NOTE:1] emerged to encounter us in battle at Jahaz,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “people.”
Jahaz. This is probably Khirbet el-Medeiyineh. See J. Dearman, “The Levitical Cities of Reuben and Moabite Toponymy,” BASOR 276 (1984): 55-57.

verses.zh: 耶和华―我们的　神将他交给我们，我们就把他和他的儿子，并他的众民，都击杀了。
verses.en: the Lord our God delivered him over to us and we struck him down, along with his sons[NOTE:1] and everyone else.[NOTE:2]
notes: The translation follows the Qere or marginal reading; the Kethib (consonantal text) has the singular, “his son.”
Heb “all his people.”

verses.zh: 我们夺了他的一切城邑，将有人烟的各城，连女人带孩子，尽都毁灭，没有留下一个。
verses.en: At that time we seized all his cities and put every one of them[NOTE:1] under divine judgment,[NOTE:2] including even the women and children; we left no survivors.
notes: Heb “every city of men.” This apparently identifies the cities as inhabited.

Divine judgment refers to God’s designation of certain persons, places, and things as objects of his special wrath and judgment because, in his omniscience, he knows them to be impure and hopelessly unrepentant.tn Heb “under the ban” (נַחֲרֵם, nakharem). The verb employed is חָרַם (kharam, usually in the Hiphil) and the associated noun is חֵרֶם (kherem). See J. Naudé, NIDOTTE, 2:276-77, and, for a more thorough discussion, Susan Niditch, War in the Hebrew Bible, 28-77.

verses.zh: 惟有牲畜和所夺的各城，并其中的财物，都取为自己的掠物。
verses.en: We kept only the livestock and plunder from the cities for ourselves.

verses.zh: 从亚嫩谷边的亚罗珥和谷中的城，直到基列，耶和华―我们的　神都交给我们了，没有一座城高得使我们不能攻取的。
verses.en: From Aroer,[NOTE:1] which is at the edge of Wadi Arnon (it is the city in the wadi),[NOTE:2] all the way to Gilead there was not a town able to resist us—the Lord our God gave them all to us.
notes: Aroer. Now known as ʿAraʾir on the northern edge of the Arnon river, Aroer marked the southern limit of Moab and, later, of the allotment of the tribe of Reuben (Josh 13:9, 16).

Heb “the city in the wadi.” This enigmatic reference may refer to Ar or, more likely, to Aroer itself. Epexegetically the text might read, “From Aroer…, that is, the city in the wadi.” See D. L. Christensen, Deuteronomy 1-11 (WBC), 49.

verses.zh: 惟有亚扪人之地，凡靠近雅博河的地，并山地的城邑，与耶和华―我们　神所禁止我们去的地方，都没有挨近。」
verses.en: However, you did not approach the land of the Ammonites, the Wadi Jabbok,[NOTE:1] the cities of the hill country, or any place else forbidden by the Lord our God.
notes: Wadi Jabbok. Now known as the Zerqa River, this is a major tributary of the Jordan that normally served as a boundary between Ammon and Gad (Deut 3:16).
